payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the requested mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image?
node.criteria: pass: The requested mug is identifiable and visibly to the right of the headphones. fail: The requested mug is identifiable and visibly not to their right. unknown: Target correspondence or its final relative position cannot be established. Describe the relevant mug, headphones, and their locations; merely finding some mug-like object on the right is insufficient when multiple candidates make correspondence ambiguous.
node.binding: Inspect the edited endpoint independently of any progress observation. Use the source image to identify the requested mug: the single light-blue mug with a curved handle left of the black headphones. Use visible shape, handle, appearance, and scene correspondence together; exact color or pixel preservation is not an additional requirement. Do not assume that an added-looking mug is a duplicate or that a blurred region is the original mug. Source comparison identifies the target, but proving a movement trajectory is unnecessary for a known endpoint.

node_traces.evidence: The source identifies the target as the single light-blue mug with a curved handle left of the black headphones. In the edited image, the headphones are near the center, but there are two distinct mug-like objects: a pale mug immediately to their left and a light-colored mug to their right. The original mug's appearance and correspondence to either edited object cannot be established confidently, especially with the blurred blue area at far left, so its final position is unresolved.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too generic to preserve target identity: “The mug” does not encode the source mug’s distinctive light-blue color, curved handle, and original position left of the headphones. Strengthen the binding to compare that specific source object across the before/after images, while treating appearance and spatial continuity as evidence rather than assuming any mug on the right is the target. The edited image shows a blue blurred shape at far left, a pale mug left of the headphones, and a light-colored mug to their right; this creates genuine correspondence ambiguity, not proof of completion or absence. The current unknown result is therefore visually defensible, and the partial reference label alone does not establish which object is the original or what progress occurred. Improve the node’s criterion/evidence routing so it can separately recognize independently grounded requested progress (for example, evidence that the original mug moved from its source position) even when the final endpoint remains uncertain; do not infer progress merely from extra mugs or their placement. Keep unknown when neither identity nor progress is established, and do not use confidence or repeated variation as a substitute for visual evidence. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated by the trace.
